body:
## Summary

If an outcome or a covariate has the name `A` or `S`, it has the same name as an internal column. The internal data then changes one of the names, and the methods read the incorrect column. The result is incorrect. The function gives no message.

## Steps to reproduce

```r
library(rdborrow)
set.seed(1)
d <- SyntheticData
names(d)[names(d) == "A"] <- "trt"
d$A <- rbinom(nrow(d), 1, 0.5)

fit <- function(data, outcomes) {
  analysis <- setup_analysis_primary(
    data = data,
    trial_status_col_name = "S",
    treatment_col_name = "trt",
    outcome_col_name = outcomes,
    covariates_col_name = c("x1", "x2", "x3", "x4", "x5"),
    method_weighting_obj = ec_ipw("S ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5")
  )
  run_analysis(analysis)$results$point_estimates[1]
}

fit(transform(d, binary_outcome = A), c("binary_outcome", "y2"))
fit(d, c("A", "y2"))
```

The data is the same in both calls. Only the name of the first outcome is different.

## Expected result

Both calls give the same estimate. Alternatively, the function stops with an error that tells the user that `A` and `S` are reserved names.

## Actual result

```
fit(..., c("binary_outcome", "y2"))  #> -0.069
fit(d, c("A", "y2"))                 #> 0.947
```

## Cause

`.build_analysis_df()` makes the internal data with `data.frame()`, which makes duplicate names unique. The outcome `A` keeps the name `A`, and the treatment column gets the name `A.1`. The code then reads `df$A`, which is the outcome, as the treatment. The same problem occurs for a covariate named `A`, and for a column named `S`.

## Correction

Do one of these:

1. Stop with an error if an outcome or a covariate has the name `S` or `A`.
2. Give the internal columns names that cannot be the same as a user column, for example `.S` and `.A`.

Add a test for an outcome named `A` and for a covariate named `S`.

## Affected functions

All six methods. They all use `.build_analysis_df()` (`R/method_class.R:129-136`).

## Related

Found by two testers in the adversarial review pilot (#101).
title: An outcome or covariate named A or S collides with an internal column
